## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the collection and analysis of water samples
for the enumeration of *Escherichia coli* (*E. coli*) and total
coliform bacteria using the IDEXX Colilert-18 / Quanti-Tray 2000
method. Results are reported as Most Probable Number (MPN) per 100 mL
[@apha2012].

This method is applicable for analyzing drinking water, surface water,
groundwater, and wastewater to assess microbial contamination levels.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Enumeration of *E. coli* and total coliform bacteria
  in drinking water, surface water, groundwater, and wastewater using
  the IDEXX Colilert-18 defined substrate method with Quanti-Tray 2000
- **Does not apply to:** Non-coliform bacterial analysis, viral or
  parasitic pathogens, or samples requiring membrane filtration methods
- **Location:** Biogeochemistry Lab and field sampling sites
- **Detection limit:** 1 MPN per 100 mL


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI / Lab Director | Approve SOP, verify and sign off on results |
| QA Manager        | Review completed bench sheets, sign lab notebook |
| Trained Personnel | Collect samples, perform analysis, record results |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Water samples may contain live microorganisms and
  pose a threat of infection. Treat all samples as potentially
  infectious.
- **Physical:** UV lamp (365 nm) can cause eye damage with prolonged
  exposure.
- **Chemical:** Colilert-18 reagent is not classified as hazardous per
  the manufacturer's SDS, but gloves and safety glasses are
  recommended.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Clean disposable nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (especially during UV reading and reagent handling)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

Water quality can range from potable to highly contaminated with
assorted pathogens. Take every precaution to protect yourself. Wash
hands frequently. In case of exposure to potentially contaminated water,
wash affected area with soap and water immediately. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Definitions

The following definitions apply throughout this SOP:

- **Analytical batch:** The set of samples processed at the same time.
- **Control cultures:** Known positive and negative cultures used to
  verify each lot of medium. *E. coli* serves as the positive control;
  *Staphylococcus aureus* serves as the negative control.
- **Field duplicate (FD):** Two samples taken at the same time and place
  under identical circumstances, treated identically through field and
  laboratory procedures. Analysis of FDs indicates the precision
  associated with sample collection, preservation, storage, and
  laboratory procedures.
- **Laboratory reagent blank (LRB):** An aliquot of sterilized water
  treated as a sample in all aspects, except that it is not taken to
  the sampling site. The purpose is to determine if analytes or
  interferences are present in the laboratory environment, reagents, or
  apparatus.
- **Laboratory duplicate (LD):** Two aliquots of the same environmental
  sample treated identically throughout a laboratory analytical
  procedure. Analysis of LDs indicates precision associated with
  laboratory procedures but not with sample collection, preservation,
  or storage.

### 6.2 Biases and Interferences

- Water samples containing humic material or other colored substances
  may interfere with visual readings. If there is background color,
  compare inoculated trays to a control tray containing only water
  (SM, 9223 A) [@apha2012].
- Chlorinated water may inhibit the growth of coliform bacteria. If the
  water has been chlorinated, use the sodium thiosulfate bottles to
  neutralize the chlorine.

### 6.3 Sample Collection

1. Arrive at the site and record site number, date, and time
2. Label the bottle with: location (geographic area and stream or lake
   name), date, time, water temperature, and sampler's initials. Label
   the bottle before immersion using a black permanent marker or
   pre-printed labels.
3. Put on latex or nitrile gloves before handling bottles. Fingers
   contain contaminants such as nitrates; bug repellent and sunscreen
   are particularly troublesome. Once gloves are on, do not touch your
   face, the ground, or anything other than the bottles.
4. Collect the sample from flowing (not stagnant) water, facing upstream
5. Immerse the bottle completely, approximately 10 cm (4 inches) deep,
   with the mouth pointing upstream so no water flows over your hand
   into the bottle. Do not allow the bottle to contact the stream
   bottom where sediments can be disturbed. Collect water 6--12 inches
   below the surface.
6. Fill the bottle to the 100 mL line on the first immersion. Pour off
   any excess and cap immediately. Do not underfill, overfill, or
   re-dunk. If too much water is poured off, use a new 100 mL
   container.
7. Do not touch the bottle mouth or inside of the cap. Be careful not
   to contaminate the sample with surface film, contact with human
   skin, or breathing into the bottle or cap. If the stream is too
   shallow to fully immerse the bottle, collect as much as possible
   while avoiding the bottom, and note the depth in field notes.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Collect one field duplicate (FD) sample every two weeks of sampling.
Duplicate sites are selected at random. The duplicate is the second
sample when two samples are collected at the same location. Duplicates
document repeatability of sample collection and reproducibility of
laboratory results.
:::

### 6.4 Sample Preservation and Storage

1. Keep samples cool during transport using a cooler with ice
2. Store at 4 C until analysis; do not freeze
3. Analyze within 6 hours of collection
4. Record the location number, bottle numbers, and collection time in
   the field sample log
5. Samples must remain in the possession of the researcher who both
   collects and analyzes them

### 6.5 Sample Processing

1. Turn on the Quanti-Tray sealer
2. Set the incubator to 35 C
3. Allow samples to reach room temperature before analysis
4. Aseptically add one packet of Colilert-18 reagent to the 100 mL
   water sample
5. Replace the lid and shake well until the reagent has fully dissolved
6. Label the Quanti-Tray with a permanent marker, recording information
   that identifies the sample
7. Open the Quanti-Tray by holding it at the top with the well side
   facing your palm. Push the top edge inward with your free hand while
   squeezing the tray into a circle. Gently pull the foil tab away from
   the plastic side. Be careful not to tear the tab. Do not touch the
   inside of the tray.
8. Pour the sample mixture into the Quanti-Tray, avoiding contact with
   the foil tab
9. Tap the small wells 2--3 times to release air bubbles. Allow foam to
   settle.
10. Place the filled Quanti-Tray on the rubber insert, making sure each
    well fits its corresponding hole
11. Push the insert with the tray into the sealer, non-foil-tab end
    first, until the sealer grabs the tray and pulls it through. If you
    need to reverse the motor, press and hold the reverse button.
    However, do not reverse the motor if the rubber insert is
    completely inside the sealer.
12. The sealer distributes the sample mixture into the wells, seals
    them, and partially ejects the sealed tray
13. Remove the rubber insert and tray from the sealer

::: {.callout-important}
If the sealer jams or malfunctions, do not force the tray. Contact the
lab manager for assistance.
:::

### 6.6 Incubation

1. Incubate the sealed tray at 35 +/- 0.5 C for 18 hours
2. Do not stack trays or block airflow around them in the incubator

### 6.7 Reading Results -- Total Coliforms

1. After 18 hours of incubation, remove the tray from the incubator
2. Count the number of large wells and small wells that are yellow and
   equal to or greater than the comparator, including the large
   overflow well at the top
3. Mark positive wells with a permanent marker as you count
4. Record the number of positive small wells and positive large wells in
   the lab notebook

### 6.8 Reading Results -- *E. coli*

1. In a darkened area, view the Quanti-Tray under the UV lamp (365 nm)

::: {.callout-warning}
### UV Safety
Be careful to avoid eye damage when using the UV lamp. Do not look
directly at the UV light source. Wear UV-protective safety glasses if
available.
:::

2. Count the number of fluorescent wells that are equal to or greater
   than the comparator
3. Record the number of fluorescent small wells and fluorescent large
   wells in the lab notebook

### 6.9 Determining MPN

1. Use the IDEXX MPN table (see Appendix) to look up the MPN based on
   the number of positive large wells and positive small wells
2. Cross-check results using the IDEXX MPN Generator software:
   <https://www.idexx.com/en/water/resources/mpn-generator/> (Windows
   only)
3. Record results on the bench sheet for both total coliforms and
   *E. coli*

### 6.10 Interpreting Results

| MPN/100 mL    | Risk Level  |
|:--------------|:------------|
| 1--10         | Low risk    |
| 11--100       | Medium risk |
| Greater than 100 | High risk |

### 6.11 Review and Sign-Off

1. The completed bench sheet should be reviewed by the researcher, the
   laboratory director, and the QA manager
2. The Lab Director or QA Manager must sign the lab notebook to verify
   that the results are accurate

### 6.12 Expected Results for Control Organisms

| Organism                  | Expected Result                  |
|:--------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| *Escherichia coli*        | Yellow wells, fluorescence       |
| *Klebsiella pneumoniae*   | Yellow wells, no fluorescence    |
| *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*  | Clear wells, no fluorescence     |
| Method blank              | Clear wells, no fluorescence     |


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### QA/QC for Each New Lot

For initial analyst demonstration of capability and for each new lot of
Quanti-Tray 2000, perform the following checks:

1. **Reagent lot check:** Shine the UV lamp on the Colilert media snap
   packs. If the unopened lot is fluorescent, discard it.
2. **Blank control:** Dissolve one packet of Colilert media in 100 mL
   of distilled water. Check for fluorescence. The blank must show no
   fluorescence.
3. **Positive control:** Dissolve one packet of Colilert media and 1--2
   Control Culture vials (stored in freezer) in 100 mL of distilled
   water. Incubate for 18 hours. Confirm fluorescence.
4. **Reagent water blank:** Analyze a sterile reagent water blank with
   each batch of samples to verify a negative result after 18--22
   hours.
5. **Sterile bottle check:** Gravimetrically check each new lot of
   sterile bottles to confirm they are transparent and non-fluorescing.

### Precision

Calculate precision for duplicate analyses using relative percent
difference (RPD):

$$
\text{RPD} = \frac{(A - B) \times 100}{(A + B) / 2}
$$

where $A$ = MPN from aliquot A and $B$ = MPN from aliquot B.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Desired precision: +/- 20% RPD
- Desired detection limit: 1 MPN/100 mL
- If a precision value exceeds 20%, record in the comments section of
  the bench sheet: "These data are associated with an out-of-control
  duplicate analysis. The UCL = 20%."
- If a blank value exceeds 1 MPN/100 mL, record in the comments
  section: "These data are associated with a blank value that exceeds
  the detection limit of 1 MPN/100 mL."
- Samples cannot be reanalyzed because the sample volume is depleted
  after the initial analysis
- If data are unacceptable for any reason, the analyst should review
  their technique before conducting this analysis again


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                        | Disposal Method                          |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used Quanti-Trays and media       | Autoclave before disposal, then standard trash |
| Used sample bottles               | Autoclave before disposal, then standard trash |
| Workspace surfaces                | Disinfect thoroughly after each session  |

::: {.callout-important}
All materials that have contacted water samples or culture media must
be autoclaved prior to disposal. Workspaces must be thoroughly
disinfected after each analytical session.
:::

## 10. Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   and [SOP-F001 Field Safety](../field_sops/SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Colilert-18 manufacturer's instructions
4. Review sampling and analysis procedures with the Lab Manager
5. Observe a trained operator perform the complete procedure (collection
   through enumeration)
6. Perform the procedure under supervision with acceptable QC results
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
